h1: R-Centric: seven luxury Dubai property experiences on one shared system
subtitle: For R-Centric we designed digital experiences for seven luxury developments in Dubai, including Omniyat projects. Each needed its own story and buyer journey; a shared system let every launch ship without starting from scratch.

cta.heading: Launching a property or a portfolio?
cta.body: Tell us about the development and the buyer. We'll show you how we'd structure the journey to a qualified enquiry.

sections.heading: Executive summary
sections.answer: Each luxury development needed a digital experience that matched its architecture and convinced a specific international buyer, without every launch starting from zero. Designit designed experiences for LIV, LIV Reside, Orla Infinity, OPUS, Vela Viento, Anwa Aria and Ela on a shared system that kept each property distinct.
body: What changed is how each site sells: location first where the area was new, daily life instead of slogans where community was the promise, and separate journeys for each audience in a mixed-use building, with enquiry flows designed to qualify buyers rather than collect form fills.

sections.heading: Project facts
items: International high-net-worth buyers; for OPUS also corporate tenants and hotel guests

sections.text: How might we give seven very different luxury properties websites as distinctive as their architecture, while buyers, enquiries and the team all benefit from one shared system?

sections.heading: Who we designed for
sections.intro: International high-net-worth buyers deciding from a screen, investors weighing location and value, and Omniyat's sales team waiting for qualified enquiries.

people.context: Judge a Dubai property online before deciding whether to visit.
Want location, availability and value made clear.
Want fewer, better-qualified enquiries with context.

painPoints: Each property had a different audience and story.
Standard contact forms felt transactional for a private purchase.

sections.heading: The business and buyer problem
paras: Every property had a different obstacle. Anwa Aria sat in an emerging area and had to overcome location scepticism. OPUS, a Zaha Hadid building, served three audiences with different goals. LIV Reside's "community living" needed proof rather than adjectives. Ela had to balance sustainability with luxury. Vela Viento's international buyers needed multiple languages and currencies, and Orla Infinity needed cinematic media without sacrificing performance.

items.title: A story per property
items.body: Research and positioning for each development's buyer, from location storytelling to lifestyle vignettes.

items.title: Journeys per audience
items.body: Multi-audience information architecture where buildings served homebuyers, tenants and guests.

items.title: Immersive, but fast
items.body: Scrollytelling, full-bleed imagery and animation, with performance optimisation for media-heavy pages and mobile.

items.title: Qualification, not capture
items.body: Comparison tools, availability and enquiry flows designed to bring serious buyers forward.

items.title: One shared system
items.body: Foundations reused across launches so each new property shipped faster while keeping its own identity.

sections.heading: Key lessons
items: Sell the location before the unit when the area is new.
Show daily life, don't claim community. Buyers discount adjectives.
Give each audience its own journey in a mixed-use building.
Qualify, don't just capture. Fewer, better enquiries serve sales teams.

items.title: UX design for Dubai and the UAE

faq.q: Which Omniyat properties did Designit design websites for?
faq.a: Seven, through R-Centric: LIV, LIV Reside, OPUS, Orla Infinity, Vela Viento, Anwa Aria and ELA Residences, each with its own case study.

faq.q: How do you keep several luxury property sites distinctive but consistent?
faq.a: Share the system, not the look: common components, navigation and enquiry flows, with each property's imagery, typography and story leading its own experience.

faq.q: Which properties did Designit design for R-Centric?
faq.a: LIV, LIV Reside, Orla Infinity, OPUS, Vela Viento, Anwa Aria and Ela, luxury developments in Dubai including Omniyat projects.

faq.q: Why a shared system across properties?
faq.a: So each new launch could ship quickly while keeping its own identity, instead of designing every property from scratch.

faq.q: What features should a luxury real estate website in Dubai have?
faq.a: Immersive photography and video, clear unit and floor-plan information, location context, multilingual content for international buyers, and an enquiry flow that feels like requesting a private consultation.
Storytelling driven by scrolling, where each section reveals the next part of the story with choreographed imagery and motion. Vela Viento uses the bay as a visual thread through the whole page.

faq.q: How do you turn property website visitors into qualified enquiries?
faq.a: Build desire first, then make the next step feel exclusive and useful: a short, multi-step enquiry that captures what the buyer wants, so the sales team receives context, not just a name.

faq.q: Do the property websites support international buyers?
faq.a: Yes. The case studies describe multi-language and, where needed, multi-currency experiences and time-zone-aware scheduling for viewings and calls.

faq.q: Where can I see each property in detail?
faq.a: Each of the seven properties has its own case study, linked above.
